-- | Hand out free <tt>localhost</tt> TCP ports for integration tests from
--   a private band below the kernel's ephemeral range, coordinated across
--   processes by file locks and verified bindable before being returned.
--   This avoids the races inherent in <tt>bind(0)</tt>-based allocation,
--   where an OS-assigned port can land on a port a test has reserved but
--   not yet bound.
@package test-network-ports
@version 0.1.0.0


-- | Utility module providing functions to find and allocate random ports.
--   
--   Ports are handed out from a private band below the kernel's ephemeral
--   range (see <a>portBandStart</a>), tracked in a process-global registry
--   so no two allocations in one test process can collide, and verified
--   free with an actual bind before being returned.
--   
--   Rationale: consumers (etcd, cardano-node, warp, ...) bind their port
--   some time after allocation, and tests that restart their subprocess
--   leave the port unbound in between. Any OS-assigned loopback port (a
--   <tt>bind(0)</tt>, or the source port of a <tt>connect(2)</tt>) handed
--   out during such a window used to be able to land on the reserved port
--   and pin it, since the kernel draws those from
--   <tt>ip_local_port_range</tt>. Allocating below that range makes the
--   windows collision-free against everything except an explicit bind of a
--   specific port in the band by a concurrent process; concurrent test
--   processes of the same user coordinate through per-port file locks (see
--   <a>tryLockPort</a>), which the kernel releases when the owning process
--   dies.
module Test.Network.Ports

-- | Lowest port handed out by the allocator. The band must sit below the
--   ephemeral range (32768 and up on Linux by default, 49152 on darwin) so
--   that OS-assigned ports can never land on an allocated one.
portBandStart :: PortNumber

-- | One past the highest port handed out by the allocator.
portBandEnd :: PortNumber

-- | All ports ever handed out (or found occupied) in this process,
--   including derived companion ports. Never released: the band is large
--   enough for any test run, and never reusing a port means a subprocess
--   still draining its listen socket cannot break a later allocation.
reservedPortsRef :: IORef (Set PortNumber)

-- | Next candidate port. Seeded from the pid so concurrent test processes
--   on one machine start in different parts of the band.
nextCandidateRef :: IORef PortNumber

-- | Warn (once) when the kernel's ephemeral range overlaps the band, which
--   would void the no-collision-with-OS-assigned-ports guarantee.
ephemeralRangeCheck :: ()

-- | Allocate one port from the band, optionally together with a derived
--   companion port. The primary (and companion, when given) are registered
--   in <a>reservedPortsRef</a> and proven bindable before being returned.
--   Ports that turn out to be occupied by something outside this process
--   stay registered, so they are never tried again.
allocatePort :: Maybe (PortNumber -> PortNumber) -> IO PortNumber

-- | Find a free TCPv4 port for listening on <tt>localhost</tt>.
--   
--   The port is unique for the lifetime of the test process, see
--   <a>allocatePort</a>.
getRandomPort :: IO PortNumber

-- | Find a free TCPv4 port and pass it to the given <tt>action</tt>.
--   
--   NOTE: Should be used only for testing.
withFreePort :: (PortNumber -> IO a) -> IO a

-- | Like <a>withFreePort</a> but also reserves the derived companion port,
--   in the same sense as <a>randomUnusedTCPPortsWithDerived</a>. Use this
--   for tests that spin up a subprocess (such as etcd) which itself binds
--   a port computed from the configured one.
withFreePortAndDerived :: (PortNumber -> PortNumber) -> (PortNumber -> IO a) -> IO a

-- | Find the specified number of free ports, mutually unique for the
--   lifetime of the test process.
--   
--   NOTE: Should be used only for testing.
randomUnusedTCPPorts :: Int -> IO [Int]

-- | Find <tt>count</tt> free TCPv4 ports such that for each returned port
--   <tt>p</tt>, the <i>derived</i> port <tt>derive p</tt> is also free
--   (and reserved alongside it).
--   
--   This is needed for tests that drive a subprocess which itself opens a
--   companion port computed from the configured one; e.g. etcd, whose
--   client port is <tt>listen - 2622</tt> in this codebase.
randomUnusedTCPPortsWithDerived :: (PortNumber -> PortNumber) -> Int -> IO [Int]

-- | All port locks taken by this process, held only to keep them reachable
--   for the process lifetime.
portLocksRef :: IORef [FileLock]

-- | Take the machine-wide lock for a port, so concurrent test processes
--   (of the same user) cannot allocate it too. The lock is an OS file lock
--   held for the process lifetime; the kernel releases it when the process
--   dies, so crashed runs cannot leak reservations. Returns False when
--   someone else holds the lock. Degrades to True (no cross-process
--   protection, the in-process registry still applies) when the lock
--   cannot be taken for any reason other than contention.
tryLockPort :: PortNumber -> IO Bool

-- | Fixed, per-user lock directory. Deliberately not TMPDIR, which differs
--   between nix shells and would defeat cross-process coordination.
portLockDir :: IO FilePath
bindSpecificLoopback :: PortNumber -> IO Socket
c_socket :: CInt -> CInt -> CInt -> IO CInt
afInet :: CInt
sockStream :: CInt
sockNonBlock :: CInt
sockCloexec :: CInt

-- | Create an AF_INET stream socket with the close-on-exec flag set
--   ATOMICALLY at creation. <a>socket</a> sets it via a separate fcntl,
--   and a subprocess spawned by a concurrent thread in the window between
--   socket() and that fcntl inherits the fd: once the parent binds the
--   shared file description and closes its copy, the subprocess keeps the
--   port bound (invisibly, as an UNCONN socket) for its whole lifetime.
--   With ~40 etcd spawns racing hundreds of sentinel sockets per suite
--   run, that window was hit regularly.
openStreamSocketCloexec :: IO Socket
